title: ArtibotLedgerEventAllowlist
description: The single source of truth for the central run ledger's event vocabulary (design ARTIBOT-5.0-DESIGN.md §3.6 '어휘 통일표'; lane 6 v5-lane6-ledger.md §5-② + §2.3). This is DATA, not a JSON Schema: `ledger-envelope.schema.json` governs the envelope, this file governs which `event` names exist and what each one's `data` must carry. Deliberately an ALLOWLIST and not a denylist -- a denylist is fail-open for every event name invented later (verification-discipline §8). An event name absent from `events` is unregistered: the writer (T-20 lib/runtime/event-writer.js) does not append it, and appends a `ledger.rejected` line carrying the original instead, then continues (design §3.6 'ledger.rejected 로 기록 후 무시'). `ledger.rejected` is itself registered here, so rejection is recorded rather than silent, and /doctor Check 8-⑤ counts those lines.

notes.sources: An event's `sources` lists which of the 8 envelope `source` values may emit it. It is always a subset of the enum in ledger-envelope.schema.json#/properties/source, which itself mirrors lib/supervisor/event-types.js:57-66 verbatim. `sources` omitted means any of the 8 -- used where the design names no emitter.
notes.required: `required` lists keys that must be present inside the envelope's `data` object. Fields already carried by the ENVELOPE (mission_id, action_id, task_id, run_id, session_id, worker, model, routing_epoch_id, idempotency_key, actor) are never repeated in `data`. Does not apply to events carrying `data_schema` -- see that note.
notes.unspecified_required: `"unspecified_required": true` marks an event the design registers by name but for which no source document states its required `data` fields. Its empty `required` is a KNOWN GAP, not a deliberate zero -- so a reader can tell the two apart instead of mistaking absence of a rule for a rule of absence. Fill these in when the owning lane specifies them.
notes.enum_ref: A `fields` entry with `enum_ref` constrains that key's value to `enums[<ref>]` when the key is present. Presence itself is governed by `required`.
notes.line_cap: `limits.line_max_bytes` is stated here so the writer reads the number from one place. It is NOT enforced by either schema: JSON Schema cannot measure the serialized byte length of the document validating against it. T-20 measures Buffer.byteLength(line, 'utf8') before append and moves the overflow into data.evidence_refs (design §3.6).
notes.required_envelope: `required_envelope` lists ENVELOPE keys (not data keys) that are optional in general but mandatory for this event -- e.g. review.completed and usage.receipt must carry the envelope `model`, worker.claimed/released must carry the envelope `worker`. Lane 6 §5-② lists these inside the event's required fields; they live at the envelope level here so one field has exactly one home, per the `required` note above.
notes.data_schema: `data_schema` names a sibling schema file in schemas/ that is the canonical contract for this event's entire `data` object, replacing `required`/`fields`. Introduced by the T-15 ↔ T-16 leader ruling for the three receipt events: design §8.2 makes the receipt AND the event data the same object, so the receipt schema is the one place that defines it. The writer validates data against that file; this allowlist does not restate its keys. Two consequences: a receipt is a self-contained document and MAY repeat envelope fields such as mission_id and session_id (the `required` note's no-duplication rule does not apply to these three), and any enum the receipt owns -- route-receipt's five-value decision.type, for instance -- is NOT copied into `enums` here.

enum_sources.review_verdict: design §3.4 'verdict 스키마 v2 = PASS|REPAIR_REQUIRED|REPLAN_REQUIRED|INTENT_REVIEW_REQUIRED|BLOCK (Hardening §15 로 확정)'. The vocabulary and the adapter from the 4 legacy vocabularies are owned by T-17; this file only records which values a ledger line may carry.
enum_sources.claim_nature: DESIGN-MODEL-POLICY-role-override.md §4.1 stratifies the refutation measurement by '작업 성격(process/judge)'. Fixed by owner decision MP-1 (ARTIBOT-5.0-DESIGN.md 부록 0-2 후속(3), 2026-09-04): '분리. 태깅은 작업 단위가 아니라 산출물(판정 문장) 단위' -- so one worker's report is `judge` because it CONTAINS a judgement, not because the assignment was called judgement work. A report can therefore be tagged only after it exists, which is why `nature` is optional on the event rather than required. `process` is mechanical grep / measurement; `judge` is consistency ruling, refutation, decision. The two values are the whole vocabulary: there is deliberately no `unknown` member, because an untagged report must be DROPPED from the denominator (§4.4 #4 '빈 값은 null 로 남기고 분모에서 뺀다') and a third enum value would let it be counted as its own stratum instead.
enum_sources.verify_result: run-ledger.schema.yaml:41 gives pass|fail. `unmeasured` is added from design §3.4 'unified-verifier status: PASS|FAIL|UNMEASURED, UNMEASURED 가 1급 상태 -- 재지 못한 층을 PASS 라 부르지 않는다'. Without it an unmeasured layer has no representable value and would have to be written as a false pass or dropped.
enum_sources.mission_status: package-v1.1/16_STATE_SCHEMA.yaml:27-35 (7종). Distinct from the Task Graph's 8 states (v1.1 7 + cancelled, Hardening §7-8), which T-14 owns.
enum_sources.human_resolved_kind: design §8.2 §19 'human.resolved{kind: correction|decision|approval}'. Scheduled for Shadow (§8.4), so declared but not required here.
enum_sources.memory_kind: lane 6 §5-④, from artifact-governance 08 '승격 대상'. The non-promotable list (transient logs, one-off retries, stale plans, provisional guesses) has no kind, so it is structurally unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged.
enum_sources.route_bind_confidence: ROUTE-RECEIPT-PRETOOLUSE-DESIGN.md §2.3-4 declares confidence exact|inferred and defines exact as 'passed tier 2', i.e. a named spawn whose prompt_id also matched. `inferred` is SPLIT here into `name` (tier 2 hit, tier 1 did not -- still deterministic) and `fifo` (nothing left to match on, probabilistic). Splitting only refines the denominator: `exact` keeps the design's meaning, so the KPI numerator is unchanged, and the two kinds of not-exact stop being one indistinguishable bucket.
enum_sources.route_bind_matched_on: MEASURED 2026-09-04, host 2.1.260 (limb l2-d1 D2 burn): an Agent-tool spawn reports agent_type === subagent_type on SubagentStart even when the caller passed a name (2/2 rows, 1/1 of them named), while team/autopilot spawns report agent_type === name (1025-row spawns.ndjson census, name-shaped values dominate). Design §2.1 recorded only the second. Tier 2 therefore matches EITHER spelling, and this field records which one actually matched -- otherwise a confidence of exact cannot be audited against the host behaviour it assumes.
enum_sources.route_bind_method: ROUTE-RECEIPT-PRETOOLUSE-DESIGN.md §2.3-4, verbatim: correlation.method = 'prompt_id+name' | 'prompt_id+fifo' | 'name-only' | 'fifo-only'. Which TIERS fired, recorded beside the confidence they produced, so a later reader can tell a promptless-but-named bind from a scoped guess without re-deriving it.

mission.created.spec: lane 6 §5-② #1. Emitted at the Intent Detection gate in scripts/hooks/runtime-prompt.js. fold start point; a mission with no mission.created is an orphan (/doctor Check 8-③).

mission.candidate_deferred.spec: design §3.1 '판정 불가면 mission 을 만들지 않고 원장에 mission-candidate-deferred'. Written with the hyphen there and normalized to the dotted vocabulary here. Carries the session fallback mission_id (M-YYYYMMDD-S<sid8>), because by definition no mission was issued. Required data fields are not stated in any source document -- lane 1 owns the substantive gate S1~S6.

intent.detected.spec: lane 6 §5-② #2. Replaces decision-events `routing-classified`, whose directory has never been created.

plan.revised.spec: lane 6 §5-② #3. fold takes the maximum revision.

route.selected.spec: design §8.2 §3·§40 'Route Receipt = 원장 route.selected 이벤트의 data. 별도 파일 아님'. Leader ruling (T-15 ↔ T-16): the receipt schema is the canonical data contract, and lane 6 §5-②'s flat keys (model, effort, reason, decision) are a pre-§8 draft and are retired. Note the shape moved too -- the receipt nests decision as decision.type, and owns the five-value vocabulary itself. Phase 0: the SubagentStart hook records a shadow receipt at spawn time (scripts/hooks/subagent-handler.js, measured 2026-09-02 18:20 -- builds the shadow RouteReceipt at :272, sets shadow_of at :298, appends at :340), so `hook` is listed alongside `scheduler`. The hook had been setting source:'scheduler' because this list allowed nothing else, and labelling the emitter as something it is not to satisfy a schema is the defect, not the fix -- the vocabulary follows the fact (T-37 precedent). `scheduler` stays for the cognitive-router path that writes the same event from Canary onward.

route.bound.spec: ROUTE-RECEIPT-PRETOOLUSE-DESIGN.md §3 'route.selected (PreToolUse) + route.bound (SubagentStart)'. STAGE 2 OF A TWO-STAGE RECORD, and it exists because the two facts arrive at different times through different events with NO shared key. The PreToolUse payload for the Agent tool is the only place the action text and subagent_type exist (host 2.1.259 binary + 2.1.260 live probe), and it does not know which agent_id will spawn; SubagentStart knows the agent_id and the policy model but carries no text. So route.selected records the receipt under the tool_use_id as a temporary epoch, and this event records the JOIN under the agent_id -- the epoch the G1 decision actually names. The first line is NEVER updated: the ledger is append-only, and an amended receipt would be indistinguishable from one that was right the first time. data.tool_use_id is the join key back to route.selected's routing_epoch_id. confidence/method say HOW the join was made, because two of the three tiers are not deterministic and a bind that does not report its own certainty is read as if it were certain (design §2.3 invariant 4). NOT REGISTERED HERE, deliberately: bind.conflict (design §2.3 invariant 1) -- the 1:1 rule is enforced by construction instead (an already-bound tool_use_id is not a candidate and an already-bound agent_id skips), so there is no conflict line to write and no event registered for one; if the reconciliation in /doctor Check 10 (design §2.3 invariant 3, 3rd batch) ever needs to report a violation rather than prevent it, that is when the event earns its entry.

model.switched.spec: lane 6 §5-② #5. Feeds Model Switch Cost. Recorded alongside route.selected{decision:'switch'} rather than instead of it (decision D7).

topology.selected.spec: lane 6 §5-② #6. Emitted by cognitive-router, autopilot, or split dispatch.

worker.claimed.spec: lane 6 §5-② #7. Written beside recordSpawn in subagent-handler. `owns[]` is the file-ownership declaration (Hardening §10: a coordination policy, not a git lock).

worker.released.spec: lane 6 §5-② #7 pairs claimed with released. Absent from the task brief's event list; registered here because the pair is what makes an unreleased worker detectable.

task.claimed.spec: design §7.2 §9 Claim/Lease/Heartbeat, lease{owner, acquired_at, expires_at, heartbeat_at}. Only claimed/released reach the central ledger; heartbeats update the store only, so a high-frequency event cannot break mission-unit rotation (decision D11).

task.released.spec: design §7.2 §9. Before GA, reclaiming an expired lease needs human confirmation.

context.compiled.spec: design §8.2 §8·§41 Context Receipt. Leader ruling (T-15 ↔ T-16): context-receipt.schema.json is the canonical data contract; lane 6 §5-②'s flat keys (supplied_tokens, cache_hit_tokens, evidence_refs) are retired. First writer is the existing lib/context/rehydration.js, which takes the ledger writer as an injected port rather than importing it (layer rule).

usage.receipt.spec: design §8.2 §4·§42 'usage.receipt 이벤트 = Attempt Receipt', Run-scoped. Leader ruling (T-15 ↔ T-16): attempt-receipt.schema.json is the canonical data contract; lane 6 §5-②'s flat keys (model, fresh_input, cached_input, output, thinking, cost_usd) are retired, and exact model identity now lives in the receipt's model_identity object rather than a bare model string. lib/economics/usage-receipt.js remains the ONLY writer, so the same spend is never counted twice.

retry.scheduled.spec: lane 6 §5-② #11. execution.retries is one of the three v1.0 run-ledger fields with no recording site anywhere today, so Retry Waste Ratio and Success@1 both start here.

review.requested.spec: lane 6 §5-② #12 states required fields for the completed half of the pair only.

review.completed.spec: lane 6 §5-② #12 with the verdict vocabulary taken from design §3.4 v2 (5 values) rather than lane 6's 3. The v1.1 §11 example writes lowercase 'pass', which is one of the 4 legacy vocabularies T-17's adapter folds into this one. verification_id joins review.md, outcome.md and the ledger (design §3.4 §5.5).

subject_agent_id.description: The reviewed agent's spawn id, when the caller has one. Not required: the spawn ledger has no mission or work-item join key (measured 2026-09-02, lib/learning/ledger/spawn-ledger.js#normalizeRecord), so an id is often unavailable and requiring it would refuse every line the Observe phase can produce.

subject_model.description: The model the REVIEWED agent ran on. Optional, and a line that does not know it OMITS THE KEY -- it does not write null. `type: "string"` is what makes that the only representable choice: the writer's matchesType would reject null, so 'unknown' cannot be smuggled in as a value that later aggregates as if it were a model. See this event's `spec` for why the value is absent before L2 D1.

nature.description: Stratum for the reviewed report. Optional by 설계 §4.4 #4: an untagged report leaves this key absent and is dropped from the denominator rather than guessed into a stratum.

claims_total.description: Denominator. `integer` only -- the >= 0 bound and the claims_refuted <= claims_total relation are NOT enforced here, because lib/runtime/ledger-schema.js#matchesType checks Number.isInteger and nothing else. lib/review/independent-reviewer.js#parseClaimAudit enforces both before a line is ever built; a line assembled by hand can still carry -1 past this file.

evidence_refs.description: Also this file's `limits.overflow_field`: when the line exceeds line_max_bytes the writer folds non-required data keys into it (see the line_cap note).

review.claim_audit.spec: DESIGN-MODEL-POLICY-role-override.md §4.2 option (iii), APPROVED as owner decision MP-4 (ARTIBOT-5.0-DESIGN.md 부록 0-2 후속(3), 2026-09-04): '측정 저장소 어휘 review.claim_audit +1 -- 예. L2 D1 착지 선행'. Records the measurement of §4.1, 'how many of a worker's claims were overturned in review': numerator claims_refuted, denominator claims_total, stratified by subject model x nature x agent definition. §4.1 also forbids the numerator alone ('분모 없는 분자는 쓰지 않는다'), which is why both counts are required together and neither is optional. The counting rule is §4.4 #2 and it is a rule for the WRITER of the document, not something this file can check: one file:line citation = 1 claim, one number = 1 claim, one judgement sentence = 1 claim. Emitted from the structured claim_audit block of a Phase 4.5 reviewer's answer, parsed by lib/review/independent-reviewer.js#parseClaimAudit. subject_model IS EMPTY UNTIL THE L2 D1 ROUTE-RECEIPT BIND LANDS -- SubagentStart carries no model (설계 §1.3), so the value comes from joining route.selected{stage:'pre'}.tool_input.model to route.bound.agent_id, and until that join exists a conforming line simply omits the key.

layer.description: Which verification layer produced this line. Optional, and deliberately carries no enum_ref: the layer vocabulary is owned by lib/verification/unified-verifier.js and duplicating it here would create a second source of truth that drifts.

verify.completed.spec: lane 6 §5-② #13. Written by dev-verify-gate / unified-verifier. The optional `layer` field (T-51 review #5) names the layer a line came from; its vocabulary lives in `lib/verification/unified-verifier.js` (exported `LAYERS`, measured at :98 on 2026-09-02 17:45 = deterministic·behavioral·operational) and is NOT restated here -- that module is free to add a layer without an allowlist edit. `required` is unchanged: a verifier that reports no layer is still a valid line, so adding the field cannot reject anything that was accepted before.

question_id.description: Opaque id of the question, identical on the human.asked line it answers. This is the join key for question-to-resolution pairing.

human.asked.spec: lane 6 §5-② #14 + design §8.2 §19. Written by the HOOK at the point it blocks (pre-bash / pre-write), not by the model -- so the model cannot omit it. That asymmetry is the point: a human.asked with no matching human.resolved is a detectable signature of 'reconstructed a guess instead of asking', and it blocks outcome.md generation (design §3.4 OD-5).

question_id.description: Opaque id of the question, identical on the human.asked line it answers. This is the join key for question-to-resolution pairing.

human.resolved.spec: lane 6 §5-② #14 requires `decision`. The task brief writes human.resolved{kind}; `kind` is declared with its enum but left OPTIONAL because design §8.4 schedules the 3-way split for Shadow, not Observe. Written by the model right after it receives an AskUserQuestion answer. T-40 measured that human.asked requires question_id while human.resolved did not even declare it, leaving asked/resolved pairs unjoinable; question_id is declared here as OPTIONAL so the join becomes expressible without widening what an existing writer may omit.

phase.ended.spec: lane 6 §5-② #16. human_wait_ms is what separates wall-clock from working time.

wallclock.started.spec: design §3.6 'phase.*·wallclock.* <- split-telemetry dual-write' and lane 6 §2.3 keep wallclock as its own pair; lane 6 §5-② instead folds split's wall-clock-* into phase.*. Following the design, which is the PRD's canonical source. Registering it costs one allowlist entry; omitting it would make the writer reject a line the design says to write.

state.updated.spec: lane 6 §5-② #17. Every writer that touches the state store appends this inside the same transaction, append FIRST and projection second. state_version increases monotonically, so a GAP in the numbering is direct evidence of a lost update -- which is how the decision-trail class of loss stops being something you only find by measuring for it (/doctor Check 8-②).

mission.checkpointed.spec: design §8.2 §21~§26 Checkpoint, written only at meaningful transitions (task completed, epoch completed, plan revised, human decision, before high risk, /save). The design specifies the Store interface (save/load/latest/list) but no event field list.

mission.completed.spec: lane 6 §5-② #18. accepted is deliberately three-valued: the writer appends {accepted:null} first and, when the observation window closes, APPENDS a second line with the verdict plus `supersedes` rather than rewriting the first (append-only; the reader takes the last value). KPI denominators count non-null only. This line is a fact derived AFTER outcome.md exists -- a ledger entry with no outcome.md is ledger contamination, not a completion (design §3.4).

mission.archived.spec: lane 6 §5-② #19. The trigger for rotation and for pruning raw logs. Rotation moves whole missions, never a line range, because a partial mission breaks fold.

memory.candidate.spec: lane 6 §5-④. The ONLY trigger is mission.completed{accepted:true} (policy promote_only_after_outcome), so a false or null outcome produces zero candidates.

memory.dedup.spec: lane 6 §5-④. Checked against existing memory files by name and description.

memory.validated.spec: lane 6 §5-④. At least one reproducible piece of evidence, or the candidate ends here.

memory.promoted.spec: lane 6 §5-④. The ledger records the promotion history only; the memory body lives in the memory file, never in the ledger.

ledger.rejected.spec: lane 6 §5-② #20. Written by the writer itself when a line fails the allowlist or the envelope. Excluded from fold and counted by /doctor Check 8-⑤. Registered in the allowlist like everything else, so the rejection path cannot itself be rejected -- and so a rejected line is recorded rather than silently dropped.
